apple.name: Apple
apple.desc: Apples, raw, with skin (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)
apple.portion: 1 medium apple (USDA: 1 medium, 3 in across = 182 g)
apple.offers: An apple is a crunchy, portable fruit with fibre (more of it in the skin) and a little vitamin C.
apple.how: Eat whole with the skin on, slice into salads or porridge, or bake or stew with cinnamon. Pair with nut butter for a more filling snack.
apple.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking apple to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of vitamin C and fibre, as part of a varied diet.
apple.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

banana.name: Banana
banana.portion: 1 medium banana (USDA: 1 medium, 7 to 7-7/8 in long = 118 g)
banana.offers: A banana is an easy, filling fruit with potassium, some magnesium and vitamin C.
banana.how: Eat as it is, slice over porridge or yoghurt, blend into smoothies, or mash into pancakes and baking. Riper bananas are softer and sweeter.
banana.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking banana to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of potassium and vitamin C, as part of a varied diet.
banana.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

avocado.name: Avocado
avocado.portion: about 1/3 of an avocado (USDA NLEA serving = 50 g)
avocado.offers: Avocado is a creamy, energy-dense fruit rich in unsaturated fat, with fibre, folate and potassium.
avocado.how: Mash onto toast, slice into salads and bowls, blend into dressings or smoothies, or eat with a squeeze of lime. A third of a fruit is a typical serving.
avocado.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking avocado to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of folate, potassium and fibre, as part of a varied diet.
avocado.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

strawberry.name: Strawberry
strawberry.portion: 140 g (USDA reference amount), about a generous handful
strawberry.offers: Strawberries are sweet, juicy berries that are an excellent source of vitamin C.
strawberry.how: Eat fresh, slice over yoghurt or porridge, blend into smoothies, or toss into salads. Frozen berries work well for cooking and smoothies.
strawberry.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking strawberry to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of vitamin C, as part of a varied diet.
strawberry.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

cauliflower.name: Cauliflower
cauliflower.desc: Cauliflower, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt
cauliflower.portion: ½ cup cooked, 1 in pieces (USDA: 0.5 cup = 62 g)
cauliflower.offers: Cauliflower is a mild, versatile vegetable with vitamin C, folate and fibre.
cauliflower.how: Roast until golden, steam, blend into soups, or break into rice-like crumbs. Curry spices and lemon suit it well.
cauliflower.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking cauliflower to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of vitamin C and folate, as part of a varied diet.
cauliflower.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

cabbage.name: Cabbage
cabbage.desc: Cabbage, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt
cabbage.portion: ½ cup shredded, cooked (USDA: 0.5 cup = 75 g)
cabbage.offers: Cabbage is a hardy, inexpensive vegetable with vitamin C, folate and plenty of vitamin K.
cabbage.how: Shred raw into slaws, sauté or braise until soft, simmer into soups, or ferment into sauerkraut. Cooking softens its sharpness.
cabbage.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking cabbage to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of vitamin C and folate, as part of a varied diet.
cabbage.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

pumpkin.name: Pumpkin
pumpkin.desc: Pumpkin, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt
pumpkin.portion: ½ cup mashed, cooked (USDA: 1 cup mashed = 245 g)
pumpkin.offers: Pumpkin is a soft, mildly sweet squash and a good source of vitamin A (from beta-carotene) with some potassium.
pumpkin.how: Roast in wedges, simmer into soup, mash into curries and stews, or fold into porridge and baking.
pumpkin.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking pumpkin to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of vitamin A and potassium, as part of a varied diet.
pumpkin.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

walnut.name: Walnut
walnut.portion: 30 g (USDA reference amount), about a small handful
walnut.offers: Walnuts are a rich, slightly bitter tree nut with plant fats, protein and fibre, plus magnesium, iron and zinc. They are energy dense, so a small handful is a typical serving.
walnut.how: Eat as a snack, chop over porridge, yoghurt or salads, or bake into bread and cakes. Store in a cool place as the oils can turn rancid.
walnut.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking walnut to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of magnesium, iron and zinc, as part of a varied diet.
walnut.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

brown-rice.name: Brown rice
brown-rice.desc: Rice, brown, long-grain, cooked (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)
brown-rice.offers: Brown rice is a whole grain that keeps its bran, which means more fibre and magnesium than white rice.
brown-rice.how: Rinse and simmer until tender, then use as a base for bowls, stir-fries and curries. Cook extra and chill for quick meals.
brown-rice.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking brown rice to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of magnesium and fibre, as part of a varied diet.
brown-rice.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.portion: 85 g, about a third of a cucumber (USDA: 1 = 85 g)
cucumber.offers: Cucumber is a crisp, watery vegetable that is very low in energy, with some potassium and vitamin K.
cucumber.how: Slice into salads, sandwiches and bowls, dip in hummus or yoghurt sauce, or pickle thinly. Keep the peel on for extra crunch and fibre.
cucumber.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking cucumber to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of potassium, as part of a varied diet.
cucumber.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

red-bell-pepper.name: Red bell pepper
red-bell-pepper.offers: A red bell pepper is a sweet, crunchy vegetable that is an exceptional source of vitamin C, with vitamin A and folate.
red-bell-pepper.how: Eat raw in strips with dips, roast until soft and sweet, or stir-fry and stuff. Having it with beans or lentils adds vitamin C, which helps your body absorb plant iron.
red-bell-pepper.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking red bell pepper to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of vitamin C, vitamin A and folate, as part of a varied diet.
red-bell-pepper.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.

green-pea.name: Green pea
green-pea.desc: Peas, green, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt
green-pea.offers: Green peas are a sweet little legume with plant protein, fibre, folate and some iron and vitamin C.
green-pea.how: Stir into risottos, soups, pasta and curries, mash with mint, or eat from the freezer, lightly cooked. Frozen peas are a handy staple.
green-pea.cycle: This profile makes no claim linking green pea to a cycle phase or to period symptoms; it is here as one source of folate, fibre and iron, as part of a varied diet.
green-pea.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS). No cycle-specific claim is made.
